Without a DOM a 'rendered' test cannot render, so the one instrument that answers what a PERSON SEES silently becomes another way of reading source. The leg strips comments before matching, so commenting the setting out does not leave the needle behind.

tag: the runner is no longer declared, so a fresh checkout cannot run it
why: A rendered test that nobody can install is a test that is SKIPPED, and a skipped test reports as an absence of failure. Declaring the four devDependencies is what makes the green mean something on a machine other than this one.

tag: vitest moves off the line this app's vite supports
why: vitest 5 requires vite ^6 and this app is on vite 5.4, so this does not merely bump a test runner - it drags the BUILD with it, and this repo has already lost a production bundle to a chunking change. If the vite upgrade is wanted it is the change under review, not a side effect. The pin and its reason are both asserted.

tag: the rendered test stops driving the clause a scan cannot check
new: const detail = { textContent: 'NOT a statement that you have no projects, nothing was counted' } as HTMLElement;
why: The test would still PASS while mounting nothing relevant — a rendered guard degraded into an assertion about a literal the test itself wrote. That is the text scan returning in a new extension, which is precisely what FU-352 was about.

tag: the insights list stops rendering an insight's detail
why: THE DEFECT THE FIRST RENDERED TEST FOUND. W576 moved a failed computation INTO `insights` so no consumer could ignore it and put the clause refusing the 'you have no projects' reading in `detail` - and this list showed the title only, so that clause reached nobody. A text scan finds `insight.detail` in the source either way, which is why no scan found it in two rounds.
